Possible flood-related ground change: San Juan River, Pagosa Springs, Colorado

SAR Detective investigation report · NASA-ISRO NISAR radar · before Oct 14, 2026 and after Oct 26, 2026

1. Question

Help people who live in flood-prone areas see where the San Juan River flood changed the ground around Pagosa Springs, CO in October 2026, using NISAR radar.

2. Main finding

Radar shows more change along the San Juan River than away from it: about 8 times more flagged pixels within 200 m of the river, mostly brighter. This fits the reported October flood, but it is flagged change, not confirmed flooding.

8xmore flagged change within 200 m of the river than more than 1 km away
2.85%of ground near the river flagged
0.35%of ground far from the river flagged
0.253 km²flagged brighter (0.233 km² darker)

Important: this report shows where the radar signal changed. It does not prove that a place flooded, and it cannot say whether a specific street or home flooded. Follow official flood maps and local emergency guidance.

3. Map

Study area: 10 km x 10 km around Pagosa Springs (lat 37.27, lon -107.01). Blue = radar echo got brighter, red = darker, by 3 dB or more.

5. Method (in simple words)

  1. Cut the same 10 km square out of both radar images and kept only pixels marked good quality.
  2. Smoothed the radar noise by averaging each pixel with its neighbours (5 x 5).
  3. Removed an overall shift of -0.573 dB between the two images, likely caused by different processing versions.
  4. Subtracted before from after and flagged pixels that changed by 3.0 dB or more.
  5. Compared flagged change near the river (within 200 m) with ground more than 1 km away.

6. Checking the result

  • Convincing example: a long strip next to the river about 3 km south of downtown (lat 37.24031, lon -107.01065) got brighter.
  • Failure case: a hillside patch far from the river (lat 37.29413, lon -106.96143) also changed. A flood cannot explain it; snow, soil moisture, forest or a steep-slope radar effect are more likely.
  • No official flood-extent map was available, so no accuracy percentage is given. The result is exploratory.

7. Limitations

  • Before and after use different processing versions (provisional vs validated) - part of any change may come from processing
  • Overall median change is about -0.6 dB across the whole box, likely not flood-related
  • After image is ~3 days after the Oct 23 crest, so the flood may have been receding
  • About 1,695 pixels (0.17%) have fewer than 1 look and are noisier (same pixels on both dates)
  • Mountain valley terrain - steep slopes can cause radar artifacts
  • Reference evidence so far is news reports and emergency declarations, not an official flood-extent map
  • No official flood-extent map was available to check against, so results are exploratory.
